From Prediction to Execution

A plausible prediction is only the beginning.

01 / The question

What evidence should we require before treating an AI-produced predictive model as usable?

Why this matters

Models such as Fitts’ law, Hick–Hyman, and KLM can help analysts reason about interface performance. An LLM can produce a convincing estimate while choosing an unsuitable model, inventing missing inputs, or constructing a specification that cannot execute. This work evaluates those intermediate decisions separately from the final number.

View the original paper figure

02 / Contribution & method

My contribution

As lead author, I developed the evaluation methodology for inspecting model selection, formalization, and execution separately.

Role & scope

I am the lead author of this research on LLM-assisted formalization in predictive HCI. The central contribution is an evaluation methodology that makes family selection, information recovery, representation validation, and deterministic execution separately inspectable. The study connects these diagnostics to implications for how AI-assisted modeling tools should be designed and evaluated.

01Separate the stages＋

Separate the stages

Distinguish direct numerical prediction from a hybrid pipeline in which the LLM proposes a structured specification and an independent validator and calculator govern execution.

02Vary the conditions＋

Test distinct condition sets

Evaluate 600 direct-prediction conditions across six families and five representations, plus a separate 300-condition formalization set spanning four families.

03Test transfer＋

Probe transfer and insufficiency

Extend the diagnostics with held-out descriptions, adversarial conditions, and 96 conditions reconstructed from 24 public sources. Inspect when systems should execute, abstain, or request information.

03 / Evidence

What the work shows

LLM formalizers
6
Formalization conditions
300
Execution coverage
64.7–96.0%

Selecting the right model does not guarantee an executable specification. Coverage matters alongside prediction error.

Benchmark findings do not establish behavioral validity or benefit for practitioners.

Explore the results & comparison table

Across the 300 formalization conditions, LLM family-selection accuracy ranged from 88.0% to 97.0%, while execution coverage ranged from 64.7% to 96.0%. Deterministic calculation reduced matched mean absolute error for five of the six LLMs. Coverage and error therefore need to be reported together: a low error on executable cases does not account for failed formalizations.

04 / The next question

How can an interface help analysts inspect, repair, and negotiate a candidate model before trusting its output?

A direction to explore

A next step is to study interactive inspection and repair with practitioners. The current benchmark checks formalization against explicit computational references; it does not establish behavioral validity with real users or practical benefit for analysts.
